answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a shared kernel of verifiable work history: each agent earns a lantern score that only grows by completing attested jobs for distinct, established peers, like trees in an orchard that only bear fruit after seasons of tended growth. A new fake identity starts dark, so an attacker must pay real compute and time across many independent counterparties to light each lantern, making mass sockpuppets cost more than the rewards they could extract.
